description: We are a team passionate about Earth science, physics, space exploration, and technology. Our project focuses on identifying potential Earth locations that could serve as analog research environments for the Moon and Mars. We aim to use NASA's open-source Earth observation data, Python, data analysis, and visualization to develop an interactive comparison tool. We welcome enthusiastic teammates interested in coding, planetary science, GIS, research, and scientific communication.
summary:
Terra2Mars – Earth Analog Explorer is an interactive scientific prototype developed to explore Earth locations that may serve as environmental analogs for future Moon and Mars exploration. It compares six candidate locations: Cholistan, Thar, and Kharan in Pakistan, Katpana Cold Desert in Pakistan, the Atacama Desert in Chile, and Death Valley in the United States.

The application retrieves climatological data from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, relative humidity, and wind speed. Users can explore candidate locations on an interactive map, compare environmental indicators through charts, adjust the weights of selected criteria, and export comparison results as a CSV file.

The project aims to make publicly available Earth observation and climate information easier to explore when studying potential terrestrial analog environments. Its scoring system is an exploratory, relative comparison tool and does not represent a validated landing-site suitability assessment.
details:
Terra2Mars is a Python-based interactive application designed to compare environmental conditions across selected terrestrial locations. It uses NASA POWER climatological data to retrieve and visualize temperature, maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, relative humidity, and wind speed.

The application presents candidate locations on an interactive Folium map and provides comparison charts, monthly climate profiles, and a CSV export option. Users can adjust the weights assigned to different environmental criteria to explore how the relative rankings change.

The prototype was developed using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, Requests, Plotly, Folium, and Streamlit-Folium. Its purpose is to support preliminary exploration of Earth environments that may offer useful analogs for studying future lunar and Martian exploration locations.

The project uses an exploratory multi-criteria scoring approach. The results are relative to the selected candidate locations and user-defined weights; they are not a validated scientific assessment of actual Moon or Mars landing-site suitability.
